summary: A feature piece on art therapy and mental health outreach in a local community, centered on the Willow Creek Art Center's weekly Open Studio. It follows individuals such as Margaret Jensen, Sarah, James Cooper and volunteer Michael Thompson, and describes community events like a World Mental Health Day mural and a university workshop. It closes on integrated care with psychiatrist Dr. Anita Desai and a Patterson Foundation grant aimed at sustaining the programs.
one_line: Art therapy programs in a local community, led by Dr. Emily Rosenthal, help adults, veterans and teens heal through creative expression and partnerships.
key_facts: In late September 2023 the author visited the Willow Creek Art Center for its weekly Open Studio, a gathering of local residents seeking relief, recovery and self-discovery through art.
Dr. Emily Rosenthal, a pioneer in art therapy, has worked in the town's healing narrative for over a decade and leads the Open Studio.
Margaret Jensen, a middle-aged woman, found solace in painting while battling depression; art therapy gave her a voice when her words faltered.
On October 10th, World Mental Health Day, a month-long community art project culminated in a mural spanning the Jefferson Street underpass.
James Cooper, a veteran outreach activist, helped create the mural, which opened a new dialogue around PTSD and community support.
Sarah, a 16-year-old high schooler with social anxiety, found calm in art classes hosted by Laura Bennett on Maple Street.
Laura Bennett is a high school art teacher and part-time therapist whose projects combine art with mindfulness.

Michael Thompson, a retired corporate executive turned full-time volunteer, ensures the Open Studio never lacks materials; his mantra is "In every dollop of paint, there's potential for someone's breakthrough."
On November 14th Dr. Rosenthal led an Art and Mental Health Workshop with the local university's psychology department to inspire youth to pursue mental health careers.
Dr. Anita Desai, a local psychiatrist, advocates combining medication and therapy with creative outlets, leading to combined therapies tailored to individual needs.
The Patterson Foundation recently awarded a grant to the initiative, aimed at training more artists and mental health advocates for sustainability and accessibility.
